oneOf.description: The answer to `Hello`.
An item a call streams.
The call started what it is about: an operation, a process.
A slow reader missed `dropped` items.
The call's end: `ok` or `err`.

chain.description: The error and its causes, outermost first.

errno.description: The kernel's errno, when the kernel refused.

exit_code.description:
The CLI's exit code for it: 1 error, 2 validation, 124 timeout,
130 cancelled.

issues.description:
Validation issues, for `Validation`; a parse error is one issue
with rule `parse` and `location` `file:line:column`.

message.description: The whole message, as the CLI prints it.

netns.description: The namespace the failing call ran in.

nlink.description:
What nlink says about a failed netlink call: the `kind` of
failure, the `object` it concerns, nlink's own `context`
(innermost last) and the extended ack's `ext_ack_offset`.

EndpointImpairment.description:
The impairment of one endpoint as it is: what the topology declares,
what `impair` set at runtime, and whether it is partitioned.

ErrorCode.description: What kind of failure: what a client branches on.

oneOf.description: No such lab, node, process, snapshot.
Another operation holds the lab.
A bad request: a malformed argument, an unknown method.
The topology does not validate.
The caller may not do this.
Client and daemon speak different API majors.
The kernel refused (netlink, nftables).

ImpairmentSpec.description:
An impairment (netem), every knob optional: what `impair` sets and the
GUI's editor edits. Values are in NLL's units (`"10ms"`, `"1%"`,
`"100mbit"`).

rx_bps.description:
Receive rate in **bits** per second — the unit [`format_rate`]
expects. nlink's rate over the time between the previous tick's
read of the link counters and this one's
(`RunningLab::diagnose_since`); `0` on the first sample for an
interface and on any tick whose counters stepped backwards.

rx_bytes.description:
Cumulative bytes received, straight off the link's
`rtnl_link_stats64` — not from tc, which accounts nothing on the
`noqueue` qdisc an un-impaired veth carries.

Counted since the interface appeared, so a consumer can
difference two samples to get the bytes in a window it chooses
*after* the run — which a rate, already averaged over the
collector's own tick, cannot give.

Monotonic only within one interface lifetime: recreating the
interface restarts it at zero. Detect a backwards step rather
than assuming monotonicity across a whole run.

rx_pkts.description:
Cumulative packets received. See [`Self::rx_bytes`] for the
monotonicity caveat.

rx_pps.description:
Receive packets per second, over the same interval and with the
same first-sample and reset rules as [`Self::rx_bps`].

tx_bps.description: Transmit rate in **bits** per second. See [`Self::rx_bps`].

LabSummary.description: One running lab, as a list shows it.

health.description: `running`, or `stale` when namespaces it claims are gone.

revision.description: sha256 of the lab's topology: changes when an `apply` changes it.

MetricsSnapshot.description: A point-in-time snapshot of all node metrics.

wire_version.description: Wire-format version of the sender (`0` = pre-versioning backend).

sockets.description:
Top TCP flows by goodput in this node's namespace, attributed to
the owning process where resolvable (Plan 160 / nlink 0.24
sockdiag). Covers bare-namespace and container nodes alike — a
container's namespace is its init pid's, since 0.11.0. Empty when
no flow moved data between the last two collector ticks.
`#[serde(default)]` keeps the snapshot wire-compatible with
backends that predate the field.

oneOf.description: Labs that appeared, changed (counts, health) or went away.
A lifecycle event of the lab, as `events.ndjson` records it.
An interface went up or down, a process exited.
A change nobody made through nlink-lab.
The latest metrics of the lab (`crate::metrics::MetricsSnapshot`).
The lab's topology changed: fetch it again (`get_topology`).
Progress of an operation on the lab.

OpEvent.description:
One step of an operation's progress (deploy, apply, destroy, restore,
scenario, benchmark, test). `seq` orders them; `ts_ms` is the Unix time
in milliseconds.

op.description: The operation's id: it is re-attached by it.

oneOf.description: Waiting behind `position` other operations on the lab.
`kind` is `deploy`, `apply`, …; `actor` who asked (`user (uid)`).
The plan: its stages with how many ops each, and the removals.
A stage begins (`index` of `of`, from 1), with its op count.
`done` of `total` ops of the whole plan; the latest one.
A wait starts: for `what`, until `deadline_ms` from now at most.
How a wait is going (`done` of `total`, e.g. FRR adjacencies).
A message: `level` is `info` or `warn`.
A `validate { … }` assertion's result.
A scenario action at `time_ms` into the scenario.
The operation failed or was cancelled: undoing `entries` changes.
The end.

OpInfo.description:
An operation the daemon runs or ran (`list_ops`): a deploy, an apply,
a scenario…

lab.description: The lab it is about; empty for the host's (`reap_orphans`).

oneOf.description: It failed and what it had done was undone.
Behind others on its lab.
It failed and what it had done was undone.

Response.description:
The result of a call. Each request has the variant named after what
it returns; `Ok` for those that return nothing.

oneOf.description: `next` is the cursor to read on from.

Free-form reports with a documented shape (diagnose, addresses,
proc-stat, stats, plans, diffs, scenario and benchmark results).

The client left a long operation running (`detach`, or it went
away): `attach_op` follows it again.
A lifecycle operation finished; `lab` is the lab it made or changed.
An exec, a shell or a wait's command ended.
The exec's output, for a buffered exec.
Reads only.
Changes labs, runs commands in them.

SocketRateMetric.description:
One TCP flow's goodput over the last collector interval, attributed
to a process. Plain data (no nlink dependency) — the backend
collector fills it from nlink's `SocketRateTracker` +
`SocketOwnerMap`.

comm.description:
Owning process command name, or `"-"` when unresolved (a
short-lived or other-user process the `/proc` walk couldn't see).

tx_bytes_per_sec.description: Transmit goodput (application bytes/second the peer acked).
